name: action1-mcp-server
description: Unofficial community connector for the Action1 RMM API, not affiliated with or endorsed by Action1. Query your fleet from Claude; destructive calls are off by default and preview first.
long_description:
Unofficial community project, not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by Action1 Corporation. "Action1" is a trademark of Action1 Corporation.

MCP server for the Action1 RMM REST API. Hand-curated tools cover the common workflows (run PowerShell on Windows and Bash on macOS, deploy updates, reboot endpoints, follow automations to completion, CVE remediation plans, audit log search, software inventory); generated tools cover every other operation of the pinned Action1 OpenAPI spec.

Safety: tools that change state are refused unless 'Allow destructive operations' is enabled, and even then every call is a dry-run preview unless it passes dry_run:false and confirm:"YES". The model sets those two arguments itself, so keep your host's per-tool approval on for destructive tools. Account operations (users, roles, organizations, enterprise) stay disabled in this bundle. Tool results, including endpoint, user and inventory data, are sent to your AI provider as part of the conversation.

action1_base_url.title: Action1 API base URL
action1_base_url.description: Your Action1 region: https://app.eu.action1.com/api/3.0 (Europe), https://app.action1.com/api/3.0 (North America), https://app.na-2.action1.com/api/3.0 (North America 2), https://app.uk.action1.com/api/3.0 (United Kingdom) or https://app.au.action1.com/api/3.0 (Australia).

action1_org_id.title: Default organization ID
action1_org_id.description: UUID of the Action1 organization. Each tool can override via org_id.

action1_client_id.title: API client ID
action1_client_id.description: Issued in the Action1 console under Settings > API Credentials. Looks like api-key-...@action1.com.

action1_client_secret.title: API client secret
action1_client_secret.description: Shown once when the credential is issued. Store securely.

allow_destructive.title: Allow destructive operations
allow_destructive.description: Check to permit destructive tools (run scripts, deploy updates, reboot, uninstall) to actually execute. Even then, every call still requires per-call confirm:"YES" and dry_run:false. Off by default for query-only safety.
